assumptions: The donor mode chosen matches the intent: arms on the cut inserts, arms flanking the target replaces it.
The molecule's topology is as the record states.
limits: It refuses rather than guessing: no PAM in the target, arms off a linear end, an amplicon that cannot clear the arms.
No upstream produces this composite, so the golden grades the hand-offs between its sections, not an upstream's output.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: A composed package (guides, donor, screening primers, protocol, order list) whose report output is the document a bench reader follows; each part's reading is on the tool that made it.
bio.jane/contract.question: What does a complete knockout or knock-in build need: guides, an off-target census, a repair template with arms, screening primers outside the arms, the protocol, and what to buy?

description: The complete build package for a knockout or knock-in, as one object: guides inside the target, an off-target census for the chosen one within this molecule, a repair template with real homology arms, a screening PCR whose primers sit OUTSIDE the arms, the protocol in order, the fragments and oligos to buy, and every coordinate ready for the map. Two donor modes: by default the arms sit on the cut (a point insertion — the target's own sequence is kept on both sides), and with `replace_target` the arms flank the whole target and it is deleted, which is the mode for replacing one CDS with another (an empty insert then deletes the target cleanly). It refuses rather than guessing: no PAM in the target, arms that run off a linear molecule, a screening amplicon that cannot clear the arms, or a non-DNA insert; and in the default mode it WARNS when an insert lands inside the target, because that is a fusion rather than a replacement. Arm length, screening flank and guide count are yours to state, because each follows the delivery method and the organism.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

arm_length.description: homology-arm length on EACH side of the cut, in bp. A protocol decision that follows the delivery method, so there is no default: state what yours needs. The published working range is 100-800 (100-400 nt synthetic, up to ~800 bp cloned). In bp.

guides.description: how many guides to carry into the package, best-scoring first. The rest are the alternatives, not filler.

insert.description: sequence to place at the cut (a tag, a selection cassette). Leave empty for a scarless rejoin — the package then WARNS that the two screening products are the same length.

insert_name.description: what the insert is called in the protocol and on the order form.

max_mismatches.description: mismatch ceiling for the off-target search within this molecule. Advanced.

nuclease.description: the nuclease (PAM + spacer length) to scan the target for. Values: SpCas9 (SpCas9: NGG (3')), SpCas9-NG (SpCas9-NG: NG (3')), SpG (SpG: NGN (3')), SpRY (SpRY: NRN (3')), xCas9 (xCas9: NG (3')), SaCas9 (SaCas9: NNGRRT (3')), SaCas9-KKH (SaCas9-KKH: NNNRRT (3')), AsCas12a (AsCas12a: TTTV (5')), LbCas12a (LbCas12a: TTTV (5')), enAsCas12a (enAsCas12a: TTTV (5')).

primer_tm.description: target melting temperature for the screening primers [°C] — follows your polymerase and buffer. In °C. Advanced.

replace_target.description: replace the WHOLE target region with the insert, arms flanking the target — the gene-replacement donor. Off (default): the arms sit on the cut and the target's own sequence is kept on both sides of the insert (a point insertion), so this must be ON to knock one CDS in for another. Empty insert + this = a clean deletion of the target. Advanced.

restriction_enzymes.description: cloning enzymes whose recognition site must NOT appear in a spacer. Advanced.

screen_flank.description: how far OUTSIDE the arms the screening primers must bind, in bp. Not decoration: a primer inside the arms amplifies the repair template as readily as the locus, so the assay cannot tell an edited colony from plasmid carry-over. In bp.

subject.description: the molecule to edit — wire a record or name a library document; leave unset to edit the open record.

target_end.description: end of the gene to knock out (0-based, exclusive). In bp.

target_name.description: what the target is called, so every mark, primer and order line names its subject.

target_start.description: start of the gene to knock out (0-based, inclusive). In bp.

name: design_knockout_package

chosen.description: the guide the package was built around

donor.description: the repair template: both arms with their genomic spans, the insert, and the junctions to sequence across

guides.description: every guide inside the target, scored, best first

marks.description: every span this package names, ready for the map

offTargets.description: the off-target census for the chosen spacer WITHIN this molecule, with the scope stated

order.description: the fragments and oligos to buy, each with the design decision it comes from

record.description: the repair template as a sequence record, so the run leaves the user holding the thing to order

report.description: the whole package as Markdown — protocol, order form, guides, template, screening and marks — so it survives outside the transcript

screening.description: the screening PCR: the pair, the two product lengths, and the span they cover

steps.description: the protocol in the order it is done
